headline: Anthropic co-designs custom AI inference chips to bypass Nvidia GPUs
summary: The Claude maker is reportedly partnering with Samsung to manufacture its own silicon, aiming for lower costs and improved efficiency.
details: Anthropic is building an in-house chip development team to co-design its own custom ASIC processors for AI inferencing workloads. This strategic move aims to reduce reliance on costly Nvidia GPUs and improve the efficiency of its Claude models.

The company is actively hiring engineers to design these chips, with an unspecified partner for development. The move follows a trend among major AI players like Google, Meta, Amazon, and OpenAI, who are all developing custom silicon to optimize their AI operations.

While Nvidia GPUs are dominant for AI training, custom ASICs can offer a lower total cost of ownership, potentially up to 65% cheaper, and are more power-efficient for inferencing tasks. This allows AI companies to better manage the escalating costs associated with running large-scale AI models.

Although Anthropic has not officially named its manufacturing partner, reports suggest it is in talks with Samsung. Other major ASIC co-design market players include Broadcom and Marvell, with Broadcom already working with Google and OpenAI on their custom chips.

Developing custom AI chips is a complex and expensive undertaking, requiring significant investment in hardware design and software optimization. However, for companies like Anthropic experiencing explosive growth and handling large-scale government and consumer contracts, the long-term efficiency gains and cost savings make it a worthwhile endeavor.
